description.narrative: Follow-on equity investment into Euro Manganese via a private placement in exchange for a stake in the Company. In February 2022, EBRD subscribed CAD 8.5 million (EUR 5.7 million) in the share capital of Euro Manganese. The Bank's contemplated follow-on investment is split as follows: (i) committed investment of CAD 4 million (EUR 2.7 million), comprising of common shares and half a warrant for each common share and expected to be part of a CAD 10 million private placement alongside other investors, and (ii) uncommitted investment of CAD 6 million (EUR 4.0 million). The proceeds of the EBRD's investment will be passed on to EMN's subsidiary in the Czech Republic for the purpose of supporting pre-development works at the Chvaletice manganese project (the "Project"). The Project is a flagship project that will meet some of the rapidly increasing demand for HPM in Europe and will offer a local and reliable supply to European battery manufacturers. At the same time, the role of EBRD is highly additional, as the Bank's participation is expected to give positive signals to the market and provide comfort to other investors to subscribe into EMN's CAD 10 million share capital increase. The Project will also have a positive effect from a socioeconomic, environmental as well as health impact perspective, as it will remediate a polluted site through the implementation of high environmental standards and engineering practices. In addition, it is expected to support regional economic development by creating contracting opportunities for local businesses during construction and operation. The transaction is fully aligned with the Mining Sector Strategy for 2024-2028 (BDS23-148/F) as it "supports the exploration and production (primary and secondary) of metals and minerals relevant to the green energy transition" by "increasing the share of investments in the exploration phase of materials critical to the green transition" and "supporting circular economy with investments, including remediation and recycling projects". The operation remains also fully aligned with the Country Strategy for the Czech Republic (BDS/CZ/21-01(F)), which highlights the need to focus on "supporting green recovery" and "diversify and deepen financing resources" by "providing direct or indirect equity".
